title: Send data from a collector you already run

blocks.content: You already run a collector, and you don't want to change your tooling. This guide shows you how to configure it to also send the metrics it collects to Grafana Cloud, without installing anything new. The example uses Prometheus and its built-in remote write feature, but other collectors such as the OpenTelemetry Collector, Grafana Alloy, and Telegraf follow the same workflow. You get an endpoint and credentials from Grafana Cloud, add them to your collector's configuration, restart the collector, and confirm the data is arriving.
First, open the setup page for hosted Prometheus metrics.
Click **Connections** in the main menu.
Click **Add new connection**.
Search for **Hosted Prometheus** to filter the catalog.
Click the **Hosted Prometheus metrics** tile.
The setup page is open. It provides everything you need, including the destination address, a credential, and the configuration.
Now create a token and copy the configuration. You need the **Admin** role in your stack.

blocks.title: Create a token and copy the config

blocks.content: Under **Choose your use case for forwarding metrics**, select **Send metrics from a single Prometheus instance**. This guide walks that path. The other cards cover multiple or high-availability Prometheus setups, and the page adjusts its instructions if you pick one of those.

Under **Configure remote_write**, choose **Directly**. This sends metrics straight from Prometheus using its built-in remote write. Choosing **Via Grafana Alloy** installs a separate collector instead, which this guide doesn't cover.

Create a new API token. Give it a name you'll recognize and click **Create token**. The token is how Prometheus signs in to your stack, and the page adds it to the configuration snippet for you. Type nothing by hand.
Copy the configuration snippet. It's a `remote_write` block that contains the endpoint to send to, your stack's username, and the token as the password.
You have a `remote_write` block with your stack's address and credentials. That's everything this page exists to give you.
Next, add it to Prometheus on the machine that runs it.

On the machine running Prometheus, open `prometheus.yml` and paste the snippet at the end of the file. If the file already has a `remote_write` section, add the new endpoint under the existing one instead.

Restart Prometheus to load the change. On most Linux hosts, run `systemctl restart prometheus`. Your scrape configs, recording rules, and alerts don't change. Prometheus just gains a second destination.
Prometheus is forwarding every metric it scrapes to Grafana Cloud.
Finally, confirm the data is arriving.
Click **Explore** in the main menu.
Open the picker and choose the data source whose name ends in **-prom**. Every stack comes with one, and it reads the metrics you just sent.
blocks.tooltip: Every query runs against one of your connected data stores. This picker chooses which one.

blocks.content: In the query field, enter `up`. It's the simplest Prometheus query, and it returns one row per target your Prometheus scrapes.
Click **Run query**. Rows coming back means your metrics are in Grafana Cloud. If it's empty, give it a minute after the restart and run it again.
Your collector didn't change. It just sends to Grafana Cloud now, and you queried the result.

Note: What you send is what usage-based billing counts. Prometheus can filter what remote write forwards using `write_relabel_configs` in the same block, so send the metrics you use, not everything you scrape.
